answer: Behavioural drift scoring assigns each agent identity a score from the delta between its action distributions in consecutive epochs; a large shift lowers trust and throttles market access. An identity must keep its score under a fixed threshold, so a sybil cluster splitting activity across many identities generates a detectable ripple in aggregate consistency. Each split raises the signal cost because every identity must sustain plausible behaviour long enough to clear the threshold. Attackers therefore pay continuous coordination overhead per identity rather than a one-time fee.
